home_feat_atlas_desc: Compare metal microstructures as schematics; learn to identify them and measure grain size
about_atlas: compare metal microstructures such as ferrite, pearlite, martensite and graphite in cast iron as schematic drawings, with their features, how they form, how they look after etching and how to tell them apart, plus a grain size number converter and an identification quiz.
atlas_noscript: The schematics, grain size converter and quiz need JavaScript. The text can be read without it.
atlas_list_lead: {n} microstructures, grouped by how they form. Tap a drawing to open how to identify it.
atlas_entries_lead: Tap a name to open its schematic, what you see, how it forms and how to tell it from look-alikes.
atlas_frac_hypo: Steel with {c}% C: mass fraction of pearlite by the lever rule {p}%
atlas_frac_hyper: Steel with {c}% C: mass fraction of proeutectoid cementite by the lever rule {p}%
atlas_shade: Why it looks light or dark
atlas_forms: How it forms (alloy and heat treatment)
atlas_confuse: Look-alikes and how to tell them apart
atlas_link_grain: Copy link to this grain size
atlas_grain_h: Grain size (grain size number and mean grain size)
atlas_grain_cmp: The idea of the comparison method
atlas_grain_cmp_lead: Grains one number apart, drawn at the same magnification. In the comparison method you match the specimen against standard charts like these.
atlas_g_cap: Schematic. Approx. magnification ×{m} (field width {w}), the equivalent of {n} grains in the field area
atlas_g_d: Mean grain diameter (square root of mean area)
atlas_g_n100: Grains per square inch at 100× (ASTM N)
atlas_g_count: Count the grains in the drawing
atlas_g_jeff: Planimetric: {i} grains inside + {c} grains cut by the frame × 1/2 + 1 for the corners = {n}. Divided by the field area {a} mm² gives {na} grains/mm² → G = {g}
atlas_g_icpt: Intercept: total test line length (dashed) {L} mm with {p} grain boundary intersections → ℓ̄ = {l} mm → G = {g}
atlas_g_count_note: The drawing uses {na} grains per mm² (the equivalent of {n} grains in the field area), and the grains continue beyond the frame. The counts give slightly different numbers because only a limited number of grains is counted and because of the grain shapes (see the note below).
atlas_practice_lead: Look at the schematic and choose the microstructure. After you answer you get the identification clues and how to tell it from the one you chose. The drawing changes a little every time.
